EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Budgeted liquidity measures financial runway after allowing for continued innovation spending. The two-stage profitability funnel requires the tangible-plus-intangible capital base to produce gross profit and for that profit to survive downstream costs as operating cash.

REASONING: The valuation leg prices conservative residual cash after asset consumption, while the quality legs decompose post-depreciation profitability into gross-profit production and operating conversion. Requiring both stages avoids treating maintenance-adjusted cash yield as attractive when it comes from a weak or deteriorating operating franchise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Innovation-Funding Residual Payback---
VERDICT: flag

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash-Backed Gross-Profit Scalability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt,cogs),at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(revt,cogs),1),LAG(revt,1)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-backed firms outperform when gross-profit productivity is high and incremental gross profit is large relative to the prior sales base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Gross profit to assets measures the existing franchise profit pool, while gross-profit change scaled by lagged revenue measures incremental pricing and production economics. This replaces the stacked DuPont and cash-conversion hurdles with a distinct gross-profit scalability mechanism requiring both level and incremental strength.

NAME: Reliable Innovation Surprise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),1),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),3),VOL(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),3)),1)))

NAME: Reliable Residual-Margin Earnings Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,ADD(dp,xint)),revt),3),VOL(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,ADD(dp,xint)),revt),3)),1)))

EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Profit after depreciation and interest scaled by revenue measures the recurring operating margin available after physical and financing burdens. Its matched mean-minus-volatility form targets residual-margin reliability without adding another binding leg to an archived capital-payoff signal.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Capital-Charge Productivity Cash Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(dp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)))),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating-cash-flow-yield firms outperform when R&D-adjusted operating profit is large relative to current physical and intangible capital charges.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Depreciation plus R&D represents the current accounting burden from physical asset consumption and intangible investment, while adding R&D back to operating income corrects the corresponding expensing distortion. The ratio therefore tests current profit earned per dollar of combined capital charge rather than reusing a level-and-change total-capital construct.

EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf,dp),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp,at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(oiadp,1),LAG(revt,1)),RATIO(DELTA(xsga,1),LAG(revt,1))),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high maintenance-adjusted cash yield outperform when current operating profitability is strong and incremental operating income exceeds incremental overhead burden.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Operating-income growth less SG&A growth, scaled by lagged revenue, measures whether additional overhead is translating into scalable profit rather than simply being cut. The current operating-return hurdle prevents temporary cost contraction or recovery from a loss base from driving the interaction.
